title: Remind users before a subscription charges them

defects.what: Each charge is counted from the previous charge, so a plan started on the 31st drifts to the 28th or 29th for good after February.

edits.find:
n = 0
    while True:
        yield nth_billing_date(sub, n)
        n += 1
edits.replace:
day = sub.start
    while True:
        yield day
        day = add_months(day, 12 if sub.period == "yearly" else 1)

defects.what: A timestamp with a non-zero offset keeps its wall-clock time and is relabelled UTC, so it names the wrong moment.
A yearly plan started on 29 February raises ValueError in the next non-leap year.
Days are subtracted after converting to UTC, so a reminder across a daylight saving change fires an hour off the user's remind time.

edits.find:
local = datetime.combine(bills_on - timedelta(days=days), sub.remind_time, tzinfo=ZoneInfo(sub.tz))
    return local.astimezone(UTC)
edits.replace:
local = datetime.combine(bills_on, sub.remind_time, tzinfo=ZoneInfo(sub.tz))
    return local.astimezone(UTC) - timedelta(days=days)

defects.what: Timestamps with fractional seconds raise ValueError.
A naive now is read as the computer's local time instead of UTC, shifting the window by the machine's offset.

edits.find:
if now.tzinfo is None:
        now = now.replace(tzinfo=UTC)

defects.what: days_before=0 is treated as unset, so a same-day reminder comes three days early.

edits.find: days = DEFAULT_DAYS_BEFORE if sub.days_before is None else sub.days_before

defects.what: The window ends at midnight of the last day instead of exactly days x 24 hours after now, dropping reminders later that day.

edits.replace: end = now.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) + timedelta(days=days)
